lines.text: An ant takes three random steps along the edges of a cube.
lines.caption: An ant takes three random steps along the edges of a cube.

lines.text: How likely is it to end up at the far corner? <short pause> Let's find out!
lines.caption: How likely is it to end up at the far corner? Let's find out!

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's crack it together.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's crack it together.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: An ant stands on a corner of a cube.
lines.caption: An ant stands on a corner of a cube.

lines.text: Each minute, it walks along an edge to one of the three nearest corners.
lines.caption: Each minute, it walks along an edge to one of the three nearest corners.

lines.text: Each of those three corners has the same chance.
lines.caption: Each of those three corners has the same chance.

lines.text: What is the probability that after three minutes, it's at the corner farthest from its start?
lines.caption: What is the probability that after three minutes, it's at the corner farthest from its start?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: Let's name the corners. The ant starts at corner A.
lines.caption: Let's name the corners. The ant starts at corner A.

lines.text: The corner farthest from A is G, at the opposite end of the cube.
lines.caption: The corner farthest from A is G, at the opposite end of the cube.

lines.text: The ant takes exactly three steps. We want the chance that it ends at G.
lines.caption: The ant takes exactly three steps. We want the chance that it ends at G.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's sort the corners by how many edges they are from A.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's sort the corners by how many edges they are from A.

lines.text: B, D and E are next to A. They're one edge away.
lines.caption: B, D and E are next to A. They're one edge away.

lines.text: C, F and H are two edges away. And G is three edges away.
lines.caption: C, F and H are two edges away. And G is three edges away.

lines.text: Here's the key. The ant has only three steps, and G is three edges away.
lines.caption: Here's the key. The ant has only three steps, and G is three edges away.

lines.text: So every step must take it farther from A. If it ever steps back, it runs out of steps.
lines.caption: So every step must take it farther from A. If it ever steps back, it runs out of steps.

lines.text: Step one: from A, all three edges lead away. The chance is three over three, which is one.
lines.caption: Step one: from A, all three edges lead away. The chance is three over three, which is one.

lines.text: Step two: say the ant went to B. From D or E, the picture is just the same.
lines.caption: Step two: say the ant went to B. From D or E, the picture is just the same.

lines.text: From B, one edge goes back to A, and two go farther away. That's two over three.
lines.caption: From B, one edge goes back to A, and two go farther away. That's two over three.

lines.text: Step three: say it's at C now. Two edges go back, and only one goes to G. That's one over three.
lines.caption: Step three: say it's at C now. Two edges go back, and only one goes to G. That's one over three.

lines.text: All three steps must go right, one after another. So we multiply the chances.
lines.caption: All three steps must go right, one after another. So we multiply the chances.

lines.text: One, times two over three, times one over three,
lines.caption: One, times two over three, times one over three,

lines.text: is two over nine. That's choice C!
lines.caption: is two over nine. That's choice C!

lines.text: Here's another way. Let's count every possible walk.
lines.caption: Here's another way. Let's count every possible walk.

lines.text: Each minute, the ant has three choices. Three times three times three is twenty-seven walks.
lines.caption: Each minute, the ant has three choices. Three times three times three is twenty-seven walks.

lines.text: All twenty-seven walks are equally likely. So how many of them end at G?
lines.caption: All twenty-seven walks are equally likely. So how many of them end at G?

lines.text: Think of the edges as three directions: across, up, and in.
lines.caption: Think of the edges as three directions: across, up, and in.

lines.text: To get from A to G, the ant must go across once, up once, and in once.
lines.caption: To get from A to G, the ant must go across once, up once, and in once.

lines.text: Going the same direction twice cancels out. Then three steps can't cover all three directions.
lines.caption: Going the same direction twice cancels out. Then three steps can't cover all three directions.

lines.text: So every good walk is one order of those three moves.
lines.caption: So every good walk is one order of those three moves.

lines.text: Three choices for the first move, two for the second, one for the last. That's six walks.
lines.caption: Three choices for the first move, two for the second, one for the last. That's six walks.

lines.text: Here are all six routes, drawn on the cube.
lines.caption: Here are all six routes, drawn on the cube.

lines.text: Six out of twenty-seven is six over twenty-seven. That's two over nine. It matches!
lines.caption: Six out of twenty-seven is six over twenty-seven. That's two over nine. It matches!

lines.text: Look! Three, two, one on top, and three, three, three below. The same numbers as before.
lines.caption: Look! Three, two, one on top, and three, three, three below. The same numbers as before.

lines.text: When would you pick this way? When the walks are easy to list, it's a great double-check.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? When the walks are easy to list, it's a great double-check.

lines.text: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: One over twenty-seven is one over three, three times. It treats every step like step three.
lines.caption: One over twenty-seven is one over three, three times. It treats every step like step three.

lines.text: But step one is always safe, and step two has two good edges. There are six routes, not one.
lines.caption: But step one is always safe, and step two has two good edges. There are six routes, not one.

lines.text: One over nine is what you'd get if step two had only one good edge. But it has two.
lines.caption: One over nine is what you'd get if step two had only one good edge. But it has two.

lines.text: One over three is what you'd get if you only looked at the last step.
lines.caption: One over three is what you'd get if you only looked at the last step.

lines.text: Four over nine is what you'd get if the last step had two good edges. Only one reaches G.
lines.caption: Four over nine is what you'd get if the last step had two good edges. Only one reaches G.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. At each step, count only the edges that keep you on track.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. At each step, count only the edges that keep you on track.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Here's a sleepy ant on the same cube.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Here's a sleepy ant on the same cube.

lines.text: Each minute, it walks along one of the three edges, or it naps and stays put.
lines.caption: Each minute, it walks along one of the three edges, or it naps and stays put.

lines.text: All four choices are equally likely. What's the chance it's at G after three minutes?
lines.caption: All four choices are equally likely. What's the chance it's at G after three minutes?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. G is still three edges away, and there are still three minutes.
lines.caption: Let's check. G is still three edges away, and there are still three minutes.

lines.text: So the ant can't nap at all! Every step must move away from A.
lines.caption: So the ant can't nap at all! Every step must move away from A.

lines.text: Now each minute has four choices, not three.
lines.caption: Now each minute has four choices, not three.

lines.text: The chances are three over four, then two over four, then one over four.
lines.caption: The chances are three over four, then two over four, then one over four.

lines.text: Multiply them: six over sixty-four,
lines.caption: Multiply them: six over sixty-four,

lines.text: which is three over thirty-two.
lines.caption: which is three over thirty-two.

lines.text: Count check: four times four times four is sixty-four walks, and the same six routes work.
lines.caption: Count check: four times four times four is sixty-four walks, and the same six routes work.

lines.text: If you found three over thirty-two, amazing work!
lines.caption: If you found three over thirty-two, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: At each step, ask which moves keep you on the path, and find that chance.
lines.caption: At each step, ask which moves keep you on the path, and find that chance.

lines.text: Then multiply the chances along the path.
lines.caption: Then multiply the chances along the path.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
